_doc: Platted street corridors measured off BOTH 1834 sheets, to settle the disagreement recorded in data/traces/street_control.json: 80 ft annotated on Hathaway against Currey's 66 ft for the 1830 plat. A corridor here is the space between two block boundary lines, measured centre to centre along a traverse that starts at a committed ground-control pixel — not a second reading of the annotation, and not a hand-placed anchor per street. Two traverses per sheet since 2026-08-11: one along Lake reading the N-S streets, one down the lot column east of Canal reading the E-W streets, which the first pass measured and threw away because nothing then distinguished a Wright lot strip from a street. Pixels are the evidence and are committed as such; metres are derived from them through each sheet's own affine, and check_street_module in tools/validate.py re-derives every one of them offline on every commit. Written by tools/measure_street_widths.py, which needs the network and is therefore not part of tools/check.sh.
confidence_note: A corridor width is measured at a stated place by a stated method that anyone can re-run, which is what documented means here. What it is documented ABOUT is the sheet: the figure it supports is the width these surveys DRAW. Both sheets carry 3.7-4.5% anisotropic paper stretch, which puts about a metre of local scale error on a 24 m street — small against the 4.27 m between the two candidate figures, and large against the 0.6 m between 18 ft and 16 ft alleys. That is why the streets are settled here and the alleys are reported but not settled.

method.traverse: each traverse starts at a committed GCP pixel and runs along one axis of the plat grid, reporting every boundary line it crosses; the axes come from the modern control through the sheet's own affine
method.boundary_line: a contiguous run of the profile inked over line_frac of a band running along the line — lot numerals, block numbers, street names and the sheets' width annotations cover a fraction of it
method.classification: by measured width alone: street_min_m or wider is a street, alley_lo_m..alley_hi_m is an alley, narrower is lot subdivision. No candidate figure enters the test
method.clear_run: a street corridor is open ground from one cross street to the next, so a candidate's own centreline is followed corridor_reach_m each way over a band corridor_band_frac of its width, and the longest unbroken run of paper has to reach 65 m — pitch_lo_m less street_max_m, the shortest block face the module band allows. Sampling outside the fetched region counts as blocked. This is the test that separates a street from a strip of lots, and it does not look at the width
method.identification: a corridor takes a street's name only if that street's committed modern junction(s), projected onto the traverse through this sheet's own affine, fall within half of pitch_lo_m of its centreline — the distance at which the next corridor along would be the better match. Every identification is re-derived offline by check_street_module from across_utm, the corridor's committed centre pixel and data/traces/street_control.json
method.width: boundary line centroid to boundary line centroid, so a reading does not depend on how heavily either line was inked

candidates.tolerance_note: 4 ft is the local scale error these sheets carry (3.7-4.5% of 80 ft is 3.0-3.6 ft) rounded up, and it is deliberately less than half the 14 ft between the candidates, so the band cannot admit both. It is used for EXCLUSION: a candidate no reading comes within tolerance_ft of is not the figure these sheets draw.
candidates.reading_note: The median runs about 5 ft ABOVE the adopted 80, on both sheets, and that is recorded rather than rounded away: the corridors these draughtsmen drew are a few per cent wider than 80 ft. Paper stretch of 3.7-4.5% accounts for most of it and the placement of a pen line for the rest, so what this measurement settles is WHICH candidate — every one of the readings is at least 9 ft clear of 66, and the nearest is within 5 of 80 — and not the platted figure to the foot.

datum_exposure._doc: What adopting the corrected Wright pixel would do, computed and NOT adopted. Wright G5 is one of the eight points data/datum.json is fitted from, so correcting it moves the origin, which re-derives every coordinate in the dataset and stales every committed mesh. That is a decision with a bake attached; this file records its cost.
